column4: ### Defining Faith
column5: ### Defining Faith

column4: Faith is a commonly misunderstood and misrepresented aspect of Christianity. As the saying goes, “there is a ditch on both sides of the road”! Because the word faith is so commonly used without proper explanation in our modern Christianity, it can come to pick up erroneous definitions amplified through misunderstanding. Faith is often portrayed either as a blanketed statement of abstracted belief or as an almost mystical power or “magic,” something you possess in a specific measured and limited amount.
column5: Faith is an aspect of the Christian faith that is often misunderstood and misrepresented. As the saying goes, “There are ditches on both sides of the road”! Because in contemporary Christianity the word “faith” is used frequently without proper explanation, it is easily misunderstood and then inflated with wrong definitions. People often portray faith either as a vague and abstract assertion of belief, or as a near-mystical ability or “magic,” as though it were something you possess with a particular measure and limit.

column4: #### What Faith is Not
column5: #### What Faith Is Not

column4: Faith misrepresented abstractly has no specific conviction or persuasion. This is often evident with a bit of probing as this representation of faith cannot be made specific. If you ask, ‘what do you believe’ or ‘why do you believe’ the person with this understanding of faith often cannot clarify beyond ‘I believe’. 1 Peter 3:15 says we should be ready to give an answer for the hope that is in us.
column5: When faith is misrepresented in an abstract way, it lacks concrete beliefs or obedient trust. A little probing reveals this, because such a portrayal of faith cannot be made specific. If you ask, “What do you believe?” or “Why do you believe?”, people who think this way often can say little beyond “I believe.” 1 Peter 3:15 says we should always be ready to give a defense for the hope that is in us.

column4: Sometimes people think of faith like a magical power-but that’s not what Scripture teaches. Faith is about a real relationship built on trust. In Scripture, faith is far more dynamic and relational-it’s rooted in persuasion, trust, and confidence in God’s character and promises. It’s not an impersonal force but an engaged response to God that shapes thoughts, feelings, and actions.
column5: Sometimes people treat faith as a magical ability—but that is not what the Bible teaches. Faith is about a real relationship built on trust. In Scripture, faith is more dynamic and relational—it is rooted in trustful obedience, reliance, and assurance regarding God’s character and promises. It is not an impersonal force; it is an active response to God that shapes one’s thoughts, affections, and actions.

column5: Why are belief and obedient trust related?

column4: Our beliefs shape the way we see and interact with the world around us. Belief molds perception and precipitates our actions. This is how our minds are wired-we live based on what we believe is possible.
column5: Our beliefs shape how we view and interact with the world around us. Beliefs forge perception and give rise to our actions. This is how our minds are set—we live according to what we consider possible.

column4: #### Faith is Persuasion
column5: #### Faith Is Trustful Obedience

column4: So, what is faith? Persuasion! The Greek word ***pistis*** means persuasion, or the result of being persuaded. We are to have persuasion towards God. In English we might say faith (persuasion) ‘**in** God’. If you are married, you hopefully have faith ‘**in’** your spouse. You believe that they will do what they said they would do, and you believe that they are being authentic and genuine. This trust should extend beyond what they’ve said, to extend to them in general.
column5: So, what is faith? Persuasion! The Greek word ***pistis*** means persuasion, or the result of being persuaded. We ought to have persuasion toward God. In English we might say faith (persuasion) ‘**in** God’. If you are married, hopefully you also have ‘**in’** faith in your spouse. You believe they will do what they say they will do, and you believe they are sincere and genuine. Such trust should go beyond what they say, extending to an overall trust in who they are as a person.

column4: Developing faith, persuasion, and trust in a relationship takes time and experience. Hopefully in life you have learned how to develop a trusting relationship with another person. The principles you’ve learned that allow you to increase your trust in someone you know will also allow you can increase your faith in God. Faith in a relationship is increased over time, in experience, with consistency, and through small and large actions that build your confidence in the other person’s character and nature.
column5: Cultivating faith, persuasion, and trust in a relationship takes time and experience. Hopefully, in life you have learned how to build a mutually trusting relationship with others. The same principles that make you trust the people you know more can also increase your faith in God. Faith in a relationship increases over time, through experiences, consistency, and those actions, big and small, that build your confidence in the other person’s character and nature.

column4: ‘Faith towards God’, is relational. Relationships are built by two parties, not one. The good news about our faith in God is that God is responsible for His side of the relationship (made possible by the atoning death of Jesus, and the infilling of His spirit at rebirth), and He helps us on our side too (through the work of the Comforter - the Holy Spirit). God is doing almost all the work, our part (as we will discuss later in this chapter) is to walk *WITH* Him in obedience.
column5: ‘Faith toward God’ is relational. A relationship is built by two parties, not one. There is good news regarding our faith toward God: God takes responsibility for His side of the relationship (made possible through Jesus’ atoning death and the indwelling of His Spirit at new birth), and He also helps us on our side (through the work of the Helper——the Holy Spirit). God has done almost all the work; our part (to be discussed later in this chapter) is to walk *WITH* Him in obedience.

column4: ### Jesus Matures Our Faith
column5: ### Jesus matures our faith

column4: Jesus is the author and perfecter of our faith (Hebrews 12:2). Our faith is designed to be continually growing and expanding. We don’t reach a single point where we have enough ‘faith’, but rather our faith increases. Consider a deep and personal relationship you have in your life today. As in any relationship we don't arrive at a specific milestone where now we ‘know’ the person. We continue to know them, and increase our knowledge of them, and this refines, shapes, and grows our relationship.
column5: Jesus is the author and finisher of our faith (Hebrews 12:2). Our faith is meant to continually grow and expand. We do not arrive at a single point at which we have enough ‘faith’, but rather our faith keeps increasing. Think of a deep and personal relationship in your life today. As with any relationship, we do not reach a particular milestone and thereby ‘know’ the person. We keep getting to know them, growing in our knowledge of them, and this refines, shapes, and grows our relationship.

column4: How do we grow our faith in God? By continuing to experience Him across His many revelations, manifestations, and attributes. Again, consider a deep personal relationship in your life. You increase the depth of relationship by engaging them in different ways, in different formats, in different mediums, in different settings. You talk to them, message them, perhaps write to them. You see them individually, and in group settings. You talk about what you value, and perhaps you challenge one another. The numerous ways go on to infinity. Across these many expressions you come to know the person more deeply.
column5: How do we grow in faith toward God? By continually experiencing Him in His many revelations, manifestations, and attributes. Again, think of a deep personal relationship in your life. You deepen the relationship by interacting with the other person in different ways, different forms, different mediums, different contexts. You talk with them, send messages, and perhaps write letters. You meet them individually and also in groups. You talk about what you value, and perhaps challenge each other. The ways are countless and can extend to infinity. Through these varied expressions you come to know the person more deeply.

column4: There are two Greek words for ‘Word’ in the Bible-**logos** and **rhema**. Understanding the difference helps us see how faith grows.
column5: There are two Greek words in the Bible for ‘Word’-**logos** and **rhema**. Understanding the difference between them helps us see how faith grows.

column4: **Logos**: generally, refers to the **concept, idea, reason, or broader expression of God’s word**. It encompasses a universal, foundational truth or message and is often used to describe God’s eternal wisdom and Christ Himself as the living Word.
column5: **Logos**: Usually refers to the **concept, idea, rationale, or broader expression** of God’s word. It encompasses a universal, foundational truth or message, and is often used to describe God’s eternal wisdom, as well as Christ Himself as the living Word.

column4: **Rhema (G4487)**: emphasizes a **specific, spoken word or utterance**. It typically refers to a particular word or message given in a specific moment, especially a spoken or revealed word that applies directly to a person’s situation.
column5: **Rhema (G4487)**：emphasizes a specific, spoken word or utterance。It usually refers to a particular word or message given at a specific moment, especially a spoken or revelatory word that directly applies to an individual’s situation。

column4: *Logos* is like the entire message of a book, whereas *rhema* is like a particular passage or sentence that speaks directly to someone at a given moment. While *logos* is God’s overarching truth, *rhema* is when part of that truth is spoken to an individual in a personal, applicable way. Together, they illustrate the fullness of God’s communication: *logos* as the broad, foundational truths of God’s character and will, and *rhema* as the specific, applied word that brings that truth alive in a person’s life and situation.
column5: *Logos* is like the overall message of an entire book, whereas *rhema* is like the particular paragraph or sentence that speaks directly to someone at a given moment。*Logos* is God’s macro truth, while *rhema* is when a part of that truth is spoken to someone in a personal and applicable way。Together, the two display the fullness of God’s communication：*logos* is the broad, foundational truth about God’s nature and will, and *rhema* is the specific, applied word that makes that truth come alive in a person’s life and circumstances。

column4: ### Example of a Rhema Word in Action
column5: ### Examples of Rhema Words

column4: God promises revelation and wisdom for all those that ask. When He speaks to us, that utterance is a *rhema* word. Rhema words are from God and serve to confirm, lead, and guide us. They are not a replacement for the *logos* word, nor do they carry authority of scripture. *Rhema* words are to be judged by the same standard as prophecy or interpretation of tongues (see the chapter on the Holy Spirit for an in-depth study on this topic).
column5: God promises to give revelation and wisdom to all who ask。When He speaks to us, such speech is a *rhema* word。Rhema words come from God to confirm, lead, and guide us。They are not a substitute for the *logos* word and do not carry the authority of Scripture。*Rhema* words should be discerned by the same standards as prophecy or the interpretation of tongues（see the chapter on the Holy Spirit for a deeper study of this topic）。

column4: At several points in my career, I have prayed for divine guidance. Several years ago, I was contemplating the process of starting to look for a new opportunity and in my prayer time, I heard God say to me ‘*Just wait on me, I have an opportunity for you.’* I was starting to look for a new job because I was dissatisfied with my current role and felt frustrated. God’s word of direction ‘*wait on me’* helped me have peace and confidence in an otherwise restless season.
column5: At several points in my career, I have prayed to seek divine guidance。A few years ago, I was considering starting to look for a new opportunity, and while praying I heard God say to me: ‘*Just wait for Me; I have prepared an opportunity for you.*’ I began looking for a new job because I was dissatisfied with my current role and felt discouraged。The guiding word God gave me, ‘*wait for Me’*, helped me gain peace and confidence in a season that would otherwise have been restless and anxious。

column4: Three of four months passed, I kept working hard and faithfully, keeping my attitude positive. God would remind me, *‘wait on me’*, then His promise occurred. I had an opportunity to be promoted and received a generous wage increase.
column5: Three or four months passed, and I continued to work diligently and faithfully, maintaining a positive attitude。God would remind me, *‘wait for Me’*, and then His promise was fulfilled。I received a promotion opportunity and a substantial raise。

column4: I could have continued my job search; I could have left. I could have started somewhere new. No doubt someone else would have gotten that promotion! But because I sought the Lord’s counsel and was persuaded in His **rhema word**, I obeyed, and received the benefit. God’s words are **alive and personal**, and He promises to give us manifold and liberal wisdom (James 1:5).
column5: I could have continued job hunting; I could have left。I could have started over elsewhere。Without a doubt, someone else would have gotten that promotion! But because I sought the Lord’s guidance and was confirmed by His **rhema word**, I obeyed and benefited as a result。God’s word is **living and personal**, and He promises to give us multifaceted and abundant wisdom（James 1:5）。

column4: I have dozens if not hundreds of times where I have prayed and asked God what to do and He has given me a rhema word. Not each had the same spectacular outcome, but they all brought a sense of peace and confidence that I was obeying God and that He would work things out. They were the words I needed for the moment! Many times, when God brings a rhema word, it's from the logos. He will bring to my memory a passage of scripture, “*Fear not for I am with you!*” (Isaiah 41:10), “*By his stripes we are healed”* (Isaiah 53:5), “*Do not grow weary in doing good!”* (Galatians 6:9), manifold examples continue!

Thomas (one of the twelve) had not been with the other disciples, so had missed the appearance of the resurrected savior. Thomas believed in Jesus, and trusted his fellow disciples, but he didn’t believe that Jesus had been resurrected in bodily form; he insisted he could not actively believe it until he experienced it personally.

column4: When Jesus appeared to His disciples and calmed them down (I imagine it's quite alarming when someone appears in your midst, having come through locked doors), He spoke to Thomas. He did not criticize or blame Thomas or accuse him as part of the wicked and perverse generation seeking a sign (Matthew 16:4) but revealed Himself to Thomas.
column5: When Jesus appeared to the disciples and settled them down（I suppose it would indeed be quite alarming when someone appears among you after passing through a locked door）, He spoke to Thomas。He did not criticize or rebuke Thomas, nor did He identify him as part of the evil and adulterous generation that seeks a sign（Matthew 16:4），but rather revealed Himself to Thomas。

column4: Jesus goes on to say, ‘*blessed are they who have not seen and have believe*d’. This is not Jesus encouraging ‘blind or ignorant faith’ or rejecting the use of empirical evidence. But He is saying that we are more blessed when we can believe without the need for empirical proof. Why? If our faith, our trust, was limited to purely what we had seen empirically demonstrated, we could never have any confidence in the future work. We would have great confidence in what had been accomplished but would not walk in the peace of God for our tomorrows and for our future.
column5: Jesus then said, ‘*Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed*d’。This is not Jesus encouraging ‘blind or ignorant faith’ or denying the use of empirical evidence。Rather, it means that we are more blessed when we can believe without needing empirical proof。Why? If our faith—our trust—is limited only to what we have seen empirically verified, we will never be able to have any assurance about the works yet to come。We will have great confidence in what has already been accomplished, but we will not be able to walk in God’s peace for tomorrow and the future。

column4: ### Practical Steps for Growing Your Faith
column5: ### Practical Steps to Cultivate Your Faith

column4: Walking with God is relational, but there are skills to be learned if you want good relationships. In earthly relationships, the skills that yield the strong and secure relationships are built upon:
column5: Walking with God is about relationship, but if you want a healthy relationship, you need to learn some skills. In earthly human relationships, the skills that build strong and secure relationships rest on the following foundations:

column4: - Open and free dialogue and communication
column5: - Open and free dialogue and communication

column4: - Healthy conflict resolution
column5: - Healthy conflict resolution

column4: - Commitment
column5: - Commitment

column4: - Consistency
column5: - Consistency

column4: You must show up consistently, reveal (communicate) yourself (our thoughts and emotions), receive the other person (listen), and walk with them, if you want a strong, vibrant relationship! All these skills apply to our relationship with God.
column5: If you want a strong, vibrant relationship, you must show up consistently, reveal (communicate) yourself (our thoughts and emotions), receive the other (listen), and walk with them! All these skills apply to our relationship with God.

column4: Beyond core relational skills, there are specific practices and disciplines that will strengthen your relationship with God:
column5: Beyond core relational skills, there are specific practices and disciplines that can strengthen your relationship with God:

column4: - **Build and Maintain a Prayer Life, Listen and Communicate with God.** Regular, heartfelt prayer is essential to a close relationship with God. Through prayer, you can share your worries, joys, and gratitude, seeking His guidance and strength. (*Philippians 4:6-7*) Being sensitive to the Holy Spirit’s voice helps you discern God’s will, find wisdom in decisions, and grow in spiritual maturity. Take time for quiet reflection to hear His direction. (*Romans 8:14*)
column5: - **Establish and maintain a prayer life, listening and communicating with God.** Frequent and sincere prayer is essential for intimacy with God. Through prayer, you can share your concerns, joys, and gratitude, seeking His guidance and strength. (*Philippians 4:6-7*) Sensitivity to the Holy Spirit’s voice enables you to discern God’s will, find wisdom in decisions, and grow in spiritual maturity. Set aside quiet, reflective time to listen for His guidance. (*Romans 8:14*)

column4: - **Spend Time in Worship.** Worship is a powerful way to draw close to God, expressing love and reverence. Through praise, song, or quiet reflection, worship deepens your awareness of His presence. (*Psalms 100:2-4*)
column5: - **Spend time in worship.** Worship is a powerful way to draw near to God, expressing love and reverence. Through praise, singing, or quiet meditation, worship deepens your awareness of His presence. (*Psalm 100:2-4*)

column4: - **Read, Study, and Meditate on Scripture.** God’s Word reveals His character, promises, and instructions for life. Dedicating time to studying Scripture helps you grow in faith, understanding, and spiritual resilience. (*2 Timothy 3:16-17*)
column5: - **Read, study, and meditate on Scripture.** God’s Word reveals His character, promises, and guidance for life. Investing time in studying the Bible helps you grow in faith, understanding, and spiritual resilience. (*2 Timothy 3:16-17*)

column4: - **Obey His Commandments.** Obedience to God’s instructions demonstrates your love, respect, and trust in Him. Walking in obedience aligns your life with His purpose and brings blessings. (*John 14:15*)
column5: - **Keep His commandments.** Obedience to God’s instructions demonstrates your love, respect, and trust for Him. Walking in obedience aligns your life with His will and brings blessing. (*John 14:15*)

column4: - **Actively Attend a Local Church and Serve.** Engaging in a church community offers spiritual support, encouragement, and opportunities to serve others. Being involved helps build a sense of belonging and strengthens your commitment to God’s mission. (*Hebrews 10:24-25*)
column5: - **Actively engage in a local church and serve.** Participating in a church community brings spiritual support, encouragement, and opportunities to serve others. Being invested helps build a sense of belonging and strengthens your commitment to God’s mission. (*Hebrews 10:24-25*)

column4: - **Build Relationships with Other Believers.** Fellowship with other Christians provides accountability, encouragement, and shared wisdom. These relationships enrich your faith journey and help you grow through mutual support. (*Proverbs 27:17*)
column5: - **Build relationships with other believers.** Fellowship with other Christians provides mutual accountability, encouragement, and shared wisdom. These relationships enrich your faith journey and help you grow through mutual support. (*Proverbs 27:17*)

column4: Our ‘faith towards God’ is not a one-time occurrence for salvation but is an ongoing practice and relationship that we are supposed to cultivate our entire lives. The benefits of a trusting and beneficial relationship are incredibly numerous, but we must do the good work of fostering that trust and growth to see it thrive.
column5: Our ‘faith toward God’ is not a one-time salvation event, but an ongoing practice and relationship we should cultivate throughout our lives. The benefits of a trusting and fruitful relationship are many, but we must do the good work of nurturing that trust and growth in order to see it thrive.

column4: ## Personal Reflection Questions
column5: ## Personal Reflection Questions

column4: 1.  What does faith mean to you personally? How has your understanding of faith grown through this chapter?
column5: 1.  What does faith mean to you personally? Through this chapter, in what ways has your understanding of faith grown?

column4: 2.  Reflect on the concept of logos and rhema. Has there been a time in your life when a specific Scripture came alive for you and became a personal rhema word? How did it impact your faith?
column5: 2.  Reflect on the concepts of logos and rhema. Has there been a time in your life when a passage of Scripture came alive to you and became a personal rhema word? How did it affect your faith?

column4: 3.  How does understanding faith as persuasion rather than a mystical force shape your relationship with God?
column5: 3. How would understanding faith as conviction rather than as a mystical power shape your relationship with God?

column4: 4.  Obedience is described as the fruit of faith. Can you think of a time when your obedience to God deepened your trust in Him? What was the result?

column5: ## Small Group Discussion Questions *(20-30 minutes)*

column5: 1. **Icebreaker:** “When you think of a person of great faith, who comes to mind? Why?”

column4: 2. **Exploring Scripture:** Read Romans 10:17. What does this verse teach us about how faith grows? How can we apply it in our daily lives?
column5: 2. **Scripture Exploration:** Read Romans 10:17. What does this verse teach us about how faith grows? How can we apply it in daily life?

column4: 3.  **Faith in Action:** What does it mean for faith to produce obedience? Share examples of how obedience has strengthened your faith or someone else’s faith journey.
column5: 3. **Faith in Action:** What does it mean that faith produces obedience? Share some examples of how obedience has strengthened your faith or others’ faith journeys.

column4: 4.  **Logos and Rhema Discussion:** Discuss the difference between logos (the written word) and rhema (the revealed word). How can we position ourselves to hear and receive rhema words from God?
column5: 4. **Logos and Rhema Discussion:** Discuss the difference between logos (the written word) and rhema (the revealed word). How can we prepare ourselves to hear and receive rhema words from God?
